title: The cost of repeated data and matrix preconditioning
subtitle: Data-constrained scaling: a version extension · Shampoo
intro: One delayed version update adds corpus validation and a four-level weight-decay sweep. The Shampoo classic connects accumulated left/right gradient statistics to Kronecker preconditioning and regret. The historical classic is not counted as news.

articles.paper: Prescriptive Scaling Laws for Data Constrained Training
articles.authors: Justin Lovelace · Christian Belardi · Srivatsa Kundurthy · Shriya Sudhakar · Kilian Q. Weinberger
articles.title: Stronger regularization does not win everywhere
articles.dateNote: First posted 2026-05-02; v2 2026-11-04 18:24 EST · delayed catch-up
articles.evidence: Compared v1/v2 text and checked added Appendices E–F and Tables 20–21; not reproduced

blocks.text: With fixed data, extra training can reduce fitting error while increasing repetition damage. The existing framework adds an overfitting term to the Chinchilla (2022) form. This version adds a full FineWeb-Edu validation and λ=0.5 and 3.0. The formula is existing methodology; the table and boundary describe new evidence. [1–3]

blocks.label: One-parameter penalty: U is unique tokens, R extra epochs beyond the first and N parameter count; five base-law parameters are fitted separately [1]

blocks.text: P falls with λ, while the single-epoch base loss rises. Greater repetition tolerance therefore does not imply superiority at every budget. The added FineWeb-Edu sweep gives one-parameter P=0.02182, near FineWeb’s 0.02305: a local check across two corpora. [1]

blocks.label: Illustrative allocation: 6ND is a parameter-token FLOPs approximation; the paper uses a more flexible four-parameter penalty for configuration selection [1]

blocks.title: Boundary
blocks.text: The λ=0.1 grid differs slightly from the others, and base-law parameters are refitted for each λ. P ratios do not isolate a causal weight-decay effect. The added corpus sweep reaches 1B parameters and 16 epochs; extrapolation remains unverified. [1]

classic.title: Why a fourth root on each side?
classic.dateNote: ICML 2018 Oral; first arXiv posting 2018-02-26; version read: official ICML 2018 paper
classic.evidence: Read Algorithm 1, Section 3 proof and Section 5 setup; matrix case only, not the higher-order tensor theorem
classic.question: Along the same pretraining trajectory, how would you separate benefits of accumulated left/right statistics from those of using only the current gradient’s polar factor?

blocks.text: Full-matrix AdaGrad (2011) stores second-order statistics of flattened mn-dimensional gradients, requiring m²n² storage. Shampoo retains matrix structure and stores m²+n² left/right statistics. Its theory concerns online convex losses, not nonconvex deep-network convergence. Let Gₜ=∇fₜ(Wₜ)∈R^(m×n), with ε>0. [4–6]

blocks.tex: L_t=\varepsilon I_m+\sum_{s\le t}G_sG_s^\top,\qquad R_t=\varepsilon I_n+\sum_{s\le t}G_s^\top G_s
blocks.label: Algorithm 1: accumulated left/right Gram statistics, not Hessians [4]
Paper’s row-major flattening: vecᵣ(ΔW)=−ηHₜ⁻¹vecᵣ(G), rather than two independent inverse square roots [4]
Lemma 8 assumes each gradient has rank at most r; matrix square roots connect the full-matrix metric to Hₜ [4]
Theorem 7 uses η=D*/√(2r), convexity, rank bounds and finite comparator distance. The trace product is tr(Hₜ) [4]
Illustrative one-step identity: † denotes pseudoinversion on nonzero singular subspaces. Removing history and setting ε=0 yields the polar factor

blocks.title: Boundary
blocks.text: The last identity is a history-free limit, not an equivalence of momentum Muon and full Shampoo dynamics. Experiments add damping and periodic decompositions; implementation choices should be distinguished from the theorem. [4]
